<t0>The Setup</t0>
My own money, a commodity product, and no one to blame but the data.

AlphaMart was a hair-styling-tools store I ran on Shopify with a partner, selling cash-on-delivery in Pakistan over an eight-month run. There was no client budget to protect, which is exactly why I went back afterward and audited it as hard as I'd audit a client's account.
<t0>What The Audit Did</t0>
Reconciled every platform export against the bank, then followed the money past the ad dashboard.
<t0>Rebuilt the full funnel</t0> from Snapchat, Meta and TikTok exports and courier settlement files, down to the individual order
<t0>Traced every order from click to cash</t0>: not just "purchases," but how many of those purchases actually survived confirmation, shipping, and returns to become a delivered sale
<t0>Compared Snapchat, Meta and TikTok</t0> on cost-per-click, cost-per-thousand-impressions and real conversion, not just the ROAS each platform reports about itself
<t0>Compared three products on real delivered performance</t0>: order value against delivery rate, instead of stopping at the listed price
<t0>Split delivery failure by courier and by city</t0> to find out whether a bad delivery rate was the courier's fault or the market's
<t0>The Real Funnel</t0>
1,092 orders were paid for by the ad accounts. 523 became cash.

Ad platforms report an order the moment a customer checks out. In Pakistani cash-on-delivery, that's the start of the funnel, not the end. Nearly a third of orders were cancelled on the confirmation call before a parcel ever moved, and another fifth came back as returns.

What this showed

The pattern ran opposite to what we expected going in, the cheapest item did not deliver the best. A buyer paying more per order seems to think it through more before ordering, and follows through more often when the rider arrives.
Stock buying didn't reflect this at the time: the best-performing product was reordered the least, and the weakest was reordered the most. That's the gap the next round of buying is built to close.

<t0>What Held Up</t0>
The media buying was genuinely excellent: <t0>11 million impressions for PKR 471,193</t0>, a click-through rate of 2.19%, and video ads that held attention through nearly 40% of a 2-second view.
Confirmation-calling every order before dispatch is a habit that transfers to any store, it saved roughly <t0>PKR 78,650</t0> in courier costs that would otherwise have been spent and refunded.

We switched from dropshipping to owned stock mid-flight once it was clear dropshipping was capping how much of the operation we could actually control, the kind of call that's easy to avoid making and costly to delay.
Eight product types were tested across the run, not one, which is how the best-performing product got found at all.
<t0>What The Audit Changed Going Forward</t0>
Never sell a product that's price-anchored on Daraz or Temu, if a customer can price-check it against ten identical listings in ten seconds, you're competing on price before the ad even runs.
Judge a product on how it performs through the whole funnel, order value and delivery rate together, not on how good it looks on the product page.
Track delivery rate by city from day one, not just by courier, a 26-point gap between two cities went unnoticed for months because nobody split the data that way.
Offer a prepaid discount from week one, prepaid orders return at roughly a quarter of cash-on-delivery's rate.
Buy stock in proportion to what's already proven to sell. AlphaMart's best product got the least stock and its worst product got the most.
When a month works, put more into it, the best month of the business was followed by a 76% cut in ad spend, for reasons that had nothing to do with performance.

The account was already spending money, just not on the right things.

Smile Line Dental was already running Google Ads on their own before I took over, but the account had never been properly configured. Campaigns were targeting worldwide instead of Islamabad, where the clinic actually operates, and traffic was split across both the <t0>Search and Display Networks</t0> in the same campaigns rather than kept separate. With <t1>zero negative keywords</t1> in place, a meaningful share of the budget was going to irrelevant clicks, searches with no local intent, and low-quality Display placements, instead of people who could actually book an appointment.

On top of that, the two most important actions, form submissions and phone calls, were going completely untracked. Even the clicks that were relevant couldn't be measured against real leads, so every optimisation decision was based on clicks alone.
Rebuilt the account structure first, then layered in tracking.
<t0>Advertiser identity verification</t0>: identified and completed Google's advertiser verification on the account, which hadn't been done and put campaign delivery at risk
<t0>Account rebuild</t0>: restructured the account from the ground up: separated Search from Display and paused Display entirely, since it was consuming budget without producing enquiries
<t0>Negative keywords</t0>: built and maintained a negative keyword list to filter out irrelevant and low-intent search terms
<t0>Location targeting</t0>: set proper geo-targeting to Islamabad and the areas the clinic actually serves, replacing the default worldwide setting
<t0>Keyword strategy</t0>: researched local search terms and structured ad groups by service type (teeth cleaning, implants, whitening, etc.)
Then built the tracking layer the account never had.
<t0>Google Tag Manager setup</t0>: installed and configured GTM on the clinic's website as the single source of truth for all tracking
<t0>Form submission tracking</t0>: set up GTM triggers to fire a conversion event every time a patient submitted an enquiry form
<t0>Phone call tracking</t0>: configured click-to-call tracking so every tap on the clinic's phone number was captured as a conversion
<t0>Google Ads conversion import</t0>: linked GTM conversion events to Google Ads so the algorithm could optimise for real patient leads, not just clicks
First Ever

A properly structured, Search-only, Islamabad-targeted account with negative keywords in place, and for the first time in the clinic's history of running ads, full visibility into which ads, keywords, and campaigns were producing real patient enquiries.
